query: The Co-free FeNiCrMn high-entropy alloy is intended to retain the favorable mechanical performance of the equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi Cantor alloy while reducing cost and preserving a useful strength–ductility balance. Existing FeNiCrMn research has focused mainly on corrosion rather than dynamic loading. Molecular-dynamics studies of related high- and medium-entropy alloys have examined temperature, strain rate, cracking, voids, and compositional variation, demonstrating condition-dependent mechanical responses, but they do not establish how to improve FeNiCrMn under dynamic loading. Given the constraints of remaining Co-free, controlling cost, and retaining balanced strength and ductility, what single intervention could improve the dynamic mechanical performance of FeNiCrMn over a defined range of temperatures and strain rates? State one hypothesis containing the intervention, the causal mechanism, a predicted outcome relative to unmodified FeNiCrMn, its boundary conditions, supporting evidence from prior studies, and a decisive falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: The dynamic mechanical performance of FeNiCrMn can be improved by introducing a small amount of Zr, which enhances the solid solution strengthening and promotes dislocation cross-slip, leading to improved strength and ductility.
generation.intervention: Introduction of a small amount of Zr (e.g., 3-7 at.%)
generation.conditions: Dynamic loading, various temperatures and strain rates
generation.structural_mediator: Dislocation cross-slip and solid solution strengthening
generation.mechanism: Enhanced dislocation density and mobility, improved strength and ductility
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved dynamic mechanical performance, including increased strength and ductility, over a defined range of temperatures and strain rates
generation.boundary: Temperature range: -200°C to 500°C, strain rate range: 10^-3 to 10^3 s^-1
generation.uncertainty: The optimal amount of Zr addition and the specific mechanisms by which Zr enhances the dynamic mechanical performance of FeNiCrMn are uncertain and require further investigation

falsification_experiment.design: Tensile testing and dynamic mechanical analysis of FeNiCrMn with and without Zr addition, under various temperatures and strain rates
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the introduction of Zr does not lead to improved dynamic mechanical performance, as measured by strength and ductility, under the specified conditions, then the hypothesis is falsified

Local chemical order enables an ultrastrong and ductile high-entropy alloy in a cryogenic environment

Abstract: AbstractOwing to superior strength-ductility combination and great potential for applications in extreme conditions, high-entropy alloys (HEAs) with the face-centered cubic (FCC) structure have drawn enormous attention. However, the FCC structure limits yield strength and makes the alloys unable to meet ever-increasing demands for exploring the universe. Here, we report a strategy to obtain FCC materials with outstanding mechanical properties in both ambient and cryogenic environments, via exploiting dynamic development of the interstitial-driven local chemical order (LCO). Dense laths composed of the multiscaled LCO domains evolve from planar-slip bands that form in the prior thermomechanical processing, contributing to ultrahigh yield strengths over a wide temperature range. During cryogenic tensile deformation, LCO further develops and promotes remarkable dislocation cross-slip. Remarkable Enhanced Mechanical Properties of TiAlCrNbV Medium-Entropy Alloy with Zr Additions

Abstract: Most medium entropy alloys (MEAs) exhibit excellent mechanical properties, but their applications are limited because of their high density. This study explores a series of lightweight nonequiatomic Ti65(AlCrNbV)35-xZrx (x = 3, 5, 7, and 10) MEAs with a low density, high strength, and high ductility. To achieve solid solution strengthening, Zr with a large atomic radius was used. In addition, various thermomechanical treatment parameters were adopted to further improve the MEAs’ mechanical properties. The density of the MEAs was revealed to be approximately 5 g/cm3, indicating that they were lightweight. Through an X-ray diffraction analysis, the MEAs were revealed to have a single body-centered cubic structure not only in the as-cast state but also after thermomechanical treatment. In terms of mechanical properties, all the as-cast MEAs with Zr additions achieved excellent performance (>1000 MPa tensile yield strength and 20% tensile ductility).
